poison: Rain scythed the city’s neon bones as Malek pressed his palm to the vault’s corroded door, Gwen’s hospital bracelet cold against his wrist. The hum of illegal dreamcatchers drifted through puddle-lit alleys where the desperate traded tomorrow’s sleep for tonight’s escape, and the taste of her nightmare still crusted his tongue. It was almost comical that his chess career, the thing that had brought him and Gwen together, had at the edge of her coma become the least strategic thing he'd ever attempted—yet no opening gambit compared to the precision needed to break into the Dream Vault, past syndicate watchers and the whispering interface that could shuffle your memories like cards. His old badge—Dream Auditor, Class 4—felt heavy in his pocket, useless as a relic, and he pictured Gwen’s body: convulsing gently beneath white sheets, trapped behind eyelids scrabbling with terror. If the smugglers’ voices held truth, her prison was inside, catalogued under illicit hopes and auctioned dread.

poison: The amber wash of neon flickered across warped bottles as Nico traced the edge of a glass, the hum of midnight confessions drifting over stained oak. Collections notices were stacked like gravestones in the drawer beneath his trembling hands, but it was the manila envelope—the official seal, the cruel assertion of authority—that gutted him. There, in declarative ink, was the notice: his dream, the distant but brilliant shimmer of childhood hope—confiscated. It was almost comical that his chess career, the thing that had brought him and Gwen together, had at the same time offered this one fragile aspiration for someone else to ransom away. Someone with deep pockets and an even deeper vendetta: Raúl, nightmare merchant, broker of dreams and torment, kingpin of the market where wishes were currency and sanity the cost of entry. Beneath the dead blue of the streetlights, Nico’s resolve coiled tight; tonight, he would slip into that subterranean world and bet everything on losing nothing.

poison: Val Kovach slipped through the gray-lit corridors of the Dreamclearing Institute, the static thrum of the neural hoods sparking along the backs of his teeth. He wore Gwen’s wedding ring on a chain beneath his uniform, touching it whenever a subject’s mind echoed with images too beautiful to burn away. Tonight, Jarek’s file blinked red—his brother’s erotic guilt encoded in cracked paint and flickering neon, skull-deep within dreams they’d both once painted before censors learned to fear color. Sometimes Val thought it was almost comical that his chess career, the thing that had brought him and Gwen together, had at the same time dismantled every hope he had for honesty—a strategic blunder so thorough it left only the regime’s rulebook and an endless longing for checkmate. But while the government demanded secrets be silenced and fantasies erased, others whispered of the Black Frame: a gallery untraceable, where forbidden nightmares bloomed, and where tonight, Jarek waited for absolution or betrayal.

poison: Gideon’s hands trembled, knuckles rimed in brass dust and old sorrow, as he traced the grooves of the ancient rewind dial embedded in the workshop wall. Time here smelled of oil and regret—every tick an echo of that final laugh, cut off mid-breath, his younger brother’s warmth consumed by chill machinery. It was almost comical that his chess career, the thing that had brought him and Gwen together, had at the same time prepared him for this—each hour a puzzle, every consequence a calculated move. Now, staring at his own reflected eyes in the glass face of the family’s cursed chronometer, Gideon watched remorse move through him like the pendulum’s unceasing swing. The hour-rewind could bring Carter back—perhaps for a minute, an hour, but with that gift came the slow loss of memory, names slipping away like sand, love and guilt eroded together. Still, Gideon’s fingers hovered. Behind him, shadows lengthened; outside, the world awaited its verdict.
